# EnterpriseGlue v0.39.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.38.1`.

## Highlights

- **runtime-logging:** Adds runtime log level and category controls, ECS-aligned JSON output, and safe TypeORM query diagnostics.
- **mission-control:** Engine pickers show each engine's full friendly name on one readable line.
- **project-git-settings:** The project Git settings token guide now shows instructions only for the Git provider in use instead of listing every provider.
- **plugin-toolchain:** Build the plugin installer and manager acquisition tools with Go 1.26.11.
- **login:** A returning user who signs in with a method their account has not connected now sees a clear, stable instruction to use the method they signed up with.
- **tenant-workspace:** Reduces the work needed to open the dashboard and displays full engine names in the Mission Control engine selector.

## User and administrator impact

- Local startup no longer logs every database query. Operators can filter request, database, authentication, and configuration bundle logs by category.
- The Mission Control engine picker shows the engine name (or its host when unnamed), never a raw engine ID. The open menu widens to fit names and options are no longer clipped.
- When only GitHub is enabled, the token setup guide and placeholder no longer mention GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps.
- Plugin acquisition and signature verification retain their existing interfaces.
- The login page titles the error "This sign-in method isn’t connected to your account" and asks the person to use the method they signed up with, then connect the new one from their profile. The message stays on screen until the person acts, and the other sign-in buttons stay visible next to it. The page never names the method the account uses.
- The dashboard opens while statistics and process activity load.
- The engine selector displays engine names without internal identifiers.
- The dashboard shows a limited-access notice only when the selected engine has resource-level visibility restrictions.
- Deleted engines are removed from runtime and project import choices.
- Unavailable engines and restricted pages show a plain-language message.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Adopt the qualified installer and manager images when they are published.

## Configuration

- Set EG_LOG_LEVEL, EG_LOGGER_LEVELS and EG_LOG_FORMAT to configure application output. Set EG_DB_LOGGING and EG_DB_SLOW_QUERY_MS to configure query diagnostics separately.
- Existing environments keep pretty output unless they opt into JSON. The production Compose example enables JSON. The default database policy emits query failures only.

## Database migrations

- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Query events omit SQL text, bound values, and raw driver errors. Configuration bundle events contain fixed status and issue codes.
- No authorization change. Only the picker's labels and layout change.
- Go 1.26.11 fixes CVE-2026-97054 in the standard library linked into ORAS and Cosign.
- Remove expired scan exceptions for CVE-2026-54285 and GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 because the lockfile already resolves patched OpenTelemetry and React Router versions.
- The wording does not disclose which sign-in method an account has. Pooled providers still cannot adopt an existing account by email.
- Authorization checks continue to use current, tenant-bound grants and roles.

## Known limitations

- JSON formatting applies to the EnterpriseGlue runtime logger. Independent CLI, proxy and third-party diagnostics can use their own format.

## Rollback

- Revert the application image and remove the logging environment overrides if needed. No database rollback is required.
- Revert the application image. No data change is involved.
- Roll back to the previous host release to restore the combined token guide.
- Prefer the next qualified forward build because older image digests carry the affected Go version.
- Redeploy the previous application image.

## Validation evidence

- Focused regressions cover level precedence, JSON shape, request correlation, configuration bundle outcomes, diagnostic log collection, and the four database policies.
- All four policies passed against the compiled application data source on PostgreSQL 17. The checks confirmed that SQL text, bind values, and raw driver errors were omitted and application logs stayed active.
- Compiled PostgreSQL migration upgrades passed with historical rows retained.
- Compiled HTTP smoke verified request and trace correlation with SQL logging disabled. PostgreSQL configuration bundle apply, restart, export, and idempotent reapply passed.
- A browser test opens the engine picker with a long name and an unnamed engine and checks full names, single unclipped rows and no raw IDs.
- EngineSelector unit tests cover the one-line items and the host fallback label.
- The project Git settings component tests cover the provider-specific guide and the neutral token placeholder.
- Both image definitions verify Go 1.26.11 in the emitted ORAS and Cosign binaries before packaging them.
- A browser test covers a returning user: an unconnected provider returns a stable error with no document reload, and the connected provider then signs in.
- The OIDC route test asserts the account-link-required redirect message.
- Authorization, dashboard, and engine selector regression checks.
